text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Fourteen parliamentarians of the opposition FORD-Asili party accuse its Secretary-General Martin Shikuku of working to paralyse the party.
- Kenya's growth rate slumped to 4.6 percent in 1996 from 4.8 percent in the previous year, well below a 5.5 percent target due to inadequate rains, high cost of domestic credit and power rationing.
- Six people are wounded when anti-riot police open fire on stone-throwing mobs protesting the killing of a golf caddie in central Kenya.
- Sixteen people die when a vehicle they are travelling in plunges into the Ruiru river.
- A disease described by agricultural experts in Kenya as the "AIDS for potatoes" -- Bacterial wilt on Irish potatoes -- breaks out in the tea-growing Tigoni area in Limuru district.
- Security forces in Eldoret intensify a search for some 60 suspects who escaped from police custody on Monday.
- Kenya's first female presidential hopeful Charity Ngilu hints at her intentions to quit the Democratic Party of Kenya.
- Philip Rotino, a member of parliament from Sigor, Rift Valley, is charged with incitement and giving false information touching on national security.

- A Nairobi court learns late university student leader Solomon Muruli who died in mysterious circumstances was threatened with death if he dared identify police officers who kidnapped him. ($1=54 Kenya Shillings)
